Scenario fixture: a11ycore-button-name-present

Targets: <button>, input[type=button|submit|reset], [role="button"]. Name sources: aria-labelledby > aria-label > title (programmatic, via getAccessibleNameInfo) > input value (for input[type=button|submit|reset]) > subtree content (for <button> and [role="button"] only — NOT for input elements). Each target has a stable id btn_case_NN.

A. Baseline: mechanism priority order (eligible)

01 — FAIL: empty <button>, no name
02 — PASS: <button> with text content
03 — PASS: <button> aria-label overrides content
04 — PASS: <button> aria-labelledby
Download report
05 — PASS: <button> title
06 — FAIL: <button> content only aria-hidden (does not count)
07 — FAIL: <button> content only [hidden] (does not count)
08 — FAIL: <button> whitespace-only content
09 — PASS: input[type=submit] value provides name
10 — FAIL: input[type=submit] no value, no aria
11 — PASS: input[type=reset] value
12 — FAIL: input[type=button] no value, no aria (input has no content fallback)
13 — PASS: input[type=button] aria-label overrides missing value
14 — FAIL: role=button, no name, no content
15 — PASS: role=button, content (content fallback allowed for role=button)
Open menu
16 — FAIL: role=button, content only aria-hidden
Hidden label
17 — FAIL: aria-label empty string, content is aria-hidden=false but still no valid programmatic name — falls back to content since aria-label counted empty

B. Visible but excluded from AT (eligibility exceptions that hold either way)

FIXED: button-name-present.js previously called helpers.isAccTreeEligible(el, ctx) and treated its return value directly as a boolean, but the helper returns an object { eligible, reasons } — always truthy — so the eligibility filter never actually excluded anything. The rule now correctly reads .eligible, so the ineligibility cases below (previously excluded from this fixture to avoid asserting the buggy behavior) are exercised here.

18b — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: aria-hidden="true", no focus/IDREF exception, missing name
Explicit tabindex<0 (programmatic focus only) does not override aria-hidden.
18c — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: hidden attribute, missing name
18d — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: display:none, missing name
18e — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: visibility:hidden, no visible-descendant override, missing name
18f — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: inert, missing name
18g — NEUTRAL/INELIGIBLE: inert ancestor, missing name
19 — EXCEPTION: role=button, aria-hidden="true" but focusable => eligible, missing name => FAIL
19b — EXCEPTION: native <button>, aria-hidden="true", no explicit tabindex needed => eligible, missing name => FAIL
<button> is natively tabbable by default; the engine's aria-hidden override exception now covers <button>/<summary>/<a href> in addition to <area>/<select>/<textarea>/<input> (see isAccTreeEligible), matching real browser tab-order behavior.
23 — EXCEPTION: visibility:hidden ancestor overridden by descendant visibility:visible => eligible, missing name => FAIL

E. role=presentation exclusion behavior

26 — FAIL (eligible, still evaluated): <button role="presentation"> focusable native control, no name

F. Native <label> association

27 — NEUTRAL (PASS): icon-only button named via a wrapping <label> alongside a sibling description (found on a real site — DeviantArt's settings toggles wrap a description div and an unlabeled aria-pressed button in one <label>)

End of fixture.
